newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Three injured in attack on Cambodian TV station.
newsitem.headline: Three injured in attack on Cambodian TV station.

text.p: Unidentified armed men injured two announcers and a police guard during a raid on a television studio in southern Cambodia, police said on Monday.
Seven men went to the studio in the southern port city of Sihanoukville on Sunday night and opened fire with AK47 assault rifles and rocket propelled grenades.
They seriously wounded two announcers, slightly hurt the policeman and destroyed transmission equipment, Sihanoukville police chief Em Bunsath said by telephone.
The officer, a member of the royalist FUNCINPEC party, said an investigation had been launched. He said it might be linked to politics as there were no signs of robbery.

An Interior Ministry official, who asked not to be identified, said FUNCINPEC had earlier asked the Sihanoukville branch of state television to broadcast a speech by one of its top officials attacking the rival Cambodian People's Party (CPP) in the ailing coalition government.
He said armed men had gone to the house of the station chief and made the same demand, but he had replied that he could not do so because it was a political issue.
FUNCINPEC and the CPP formed an uneasy coalition government after U.N.-run elections in 1993.
Relations deteriorated after a March 30 grenade attack on a rally led by opposition leader and FUNCINPEC ally Sam Rainsy.
Relations reached rock bottom after co-Premier Hun Sen said his CPP supported a challenge to Ranariddh's leadership, announced in mid-April by FUNCINPEC dissidents.
FUNCINPEC has complained that it is not given the same amount of air time on state-run media as the CPP.
